Meta (Facebook / Instagram) ads: ads, campaigns, daily results

relations.name: analytics.meta_ads
relations.purpose: Dimension: one row per Meta ad (every ad the pipeline has ever seen: 42K, most ARCHIVED or DELETED) with its campaign, ad set, product, status and all-time totals. Join to the daily views on ad_id (they already carry the main names).
relations.source: public.meta_ads + meta_campaigns + meta_family_map + the product rule below + meta_ad_lifetime
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC): ad names, campaigns and totals from the Meta Graph API, status refreshed every night
relations.coverage: every ad with delivery since 2026-05-06 plus every ad the all-time pull returned; first_day / last_day only for ads that delivered since 2026-05-06
caveats: product_slug follows the Products table: a Meta family that maps to a tracker family counts under the product of that family's FIRST tracker row; a family off the tracker keeps the product guessed from its name, then campaign, then ad set; NULL = no active product. About 12K Meta families are on no tracker row.
family_key is the lower-cased ad name with ' - Copy N' and merge-tag suffixes stripped: copies of one ad share a family.

lifetime_* are Meta-reported all-time totals through the last complete day (Graph insights, both accounts, replaced nightly). They cover the whole life of the ad, not just 2026-05-06 onward; the daily views start on 2026-05-06.
status is Meta's effective_status; CAMPAIGN_PAUSED and ADSET_PAUSED mean the ad itself is on but a parent is off.

columns.name: ad_id
columns.description: Meta ad id (text, as Meta returns it).

columns.name: account
columns.description: Ad account name: 'Lonvera Main' (America/Los_Angeles) or 'Lonvera BackUp' (America/New_York).

columns.name: ad_name
columns.description: Current ad name in Meta (renames move the whole history).

columns.name: family_name
columns.description: Ad name without ' - Copy N' / merge-tag suffixes, original case: the ad family.

columns.name: family_key
columns.description: Lower-cased family_name. The join key to the creative tracker side (meta_family_map).

columns.name: tracker_family_key
columns.description: Creative-tracker family this Meta family was matched to by the resolver (NULL = no tracker row). Joins creative_tracker.family_key.

columns.name: product_slug
columns.description: vita-bull | beef-liver | boneflex | vita-belle | vital-flow | unassigned, by the rule in the view description; NULL = no active product.

columns.name: campaign_name
columns.description: Campaign name. A name containing 'test' makes the campaign a testing campaign.

columns.name: stage
columns.description: 'testing' when the campaign name contains 'test' (case-insensitive), else 'scaling'. A naming rule, not a Meta field.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Meta effective_status: ACTIVE, PAUSED, CAMPAIGN_PAUSED, ADSET_PAUSED, ARCHIVED, DELETED, DISAPPROVED, WITH_ISSUES.

columns.name: is_active
columns.description: status = 'ACTIVE' (the ad is eligible to deliver; it may still have spent nothing yet).

columns.name: created_date
columns.description: Pacific calendar date the ad was created.

columns.name: first_day
columns.description: First day with an ad_daily row (>= 2026-05-06); NULL for ads that never delivered in that window.

columns.name: last_day
columns.description: Last day with an ad_daily row.

columns.name: lifetime_spend
columns.description: All-time spend, dollars (Meta-reported). NULL when the ad has no lifetime row.

columns.name: lifetime_revenue
columns.description: All-time Meta-reported purchase conversion value, dollars.

examples.title: Active ads and their spend, by product
examples.sql:
SELECT product_slug, count(*) AS active_ads, round(sum(lifetime_spend)) AS lifetime_spend
FROM analytics.meta_ads
WHERE is_active
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

examples.title: Ads that delivered in the last 7 days but are not active now
examples.sql:
SELECT ad_id, ad_name, status, last_day
FROM analytics.meta_ads
WHERE last_day >= (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 6 AND NOT is_active
ORDER BY last_day DESC LIMIT 50;

relations.name: analytics.meta_ad_daily
relations.purpose: The main Meta fact view: one row per Meta ad per day with Meta-reported results AND Upstack-attributed new customers / orders side by side, plus the ad's names, campaign, ad set, stage and product. Roll up from here; never add purchases to Google's.
relations.source: public.ad_daily (Meta Graph API, ad x day) combined per ad and day with public.ad_daily_upstack (Upstack any-click 30-day attribution mapped to ads), names from analytics.meta_ads
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC): Meta trailing 28 days re-pulled and replaced (Meta restates conversions for weeks), Upstack trailing 7 days re-pulled
relations.coverage: 2026-05-06 through yesterday (Pacific). Meta days are each ad account's own calendar day; Upstack days are Pacific.
caveats: Three bases live in this view. spend, impressions, link_clicks, meta_purchases, meta_revenue are Meta's. upstack_new_customers / upstack_new_customer_revenue are Upstack's first-order basis (the 'NC' numbers: NC ROAS = upstack_new_customer_revenue / spend). upstack_orders / upstack_order_revenue are every order Upstack credits to the ad. Spend is Meta's in all three.
upstack_* is NULL (not 0) on days Upstack has not been pulled; coverage starts 2026-05-06 as well.

Upstack credits an order to every ad clicked in the 30 days before it (any-click), so Upstack-only ad-days exist where the ad spent nothing that day (spend = 0, meta_* = 0, upstack_* > 0). Filter spend > 0 only if you want delivery days.

When one ad is copied into several ad sets under the same name, Upstack (which sees names, not ids) credit is split across the copies by their Meta spend that day. Family-level and higher sums are exact; one copy's own upstack_* numbers are an allocation.
About 1.3% of Upstack-credited orders and 1.3% of new customers match no Meta ad ('(not set)', deleted ads); they are in orders_daily but in no row here.
Meta purchases count returning customers; Upstack new customers do not. They are different quantities, not the same number measured twice.
link_clicks is Meta's 'link_click' action count (link clicks, not all clicks). Impressions are Meta's.
source: 'meta_api' for Graph-pulled rows, 'sheet' for the old family-grain backfill (none left in production), NULL on Upstack-only ad-days.

columns.name: day
columns.description: Calendar day. Meta numbers: the ad account's own day (Main = America/Los_Angeles, BackUp = America/New_York, not re-based). Upstack numbers: Pacific.

columns.name: product_slug
columns.description: Product the ad counts under (see analytics.meta_ads); NULL = no active product.

columns.name: campaign_id
columns.description: Meta campaign id (NULL on family-grain legacy rows).

columns.name: stage
columns.description: 'testing' | 'scaling' from the campaign name ('test' in the name = testing).

columns.name: adset_id
columns.description: Meta ad set id (NULL on family-grain legacy rows).

columns.name: source
columns.description: Where the Meta side of the row came from: 'meta_api' | 'sheet'; NULL when the row exists only because Upstack credited the ad.

columns.name: spend
columns.description: Meta spend, dollars (0 on Upstack-only ad-days). Additive across ads, ad sets, campaigns and across platforms.

columns.name: meta_purchases
columns.description: Purchases Meta reports for the ad that day (omni_purchase, else purchase, else pixel purchase), Meta's default attribution; includes returning customers.

columns.name: meta_revenue
columns.description: Purchase conversion value Meta reports, dollars. meta_revenue / spend = Meta ROAS.

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: First-time customers Upstack credits to the ad (any-click, 30-day window, utm_source 'Meta Ads'). NULL on days not pulled.

columns.name: upstack_new_customer_revenue
columns.description: Order total (tax included, before refunds) of those first orders, dollars. / spend = NC ROAS.

columns.name: upstack_orders
columns.description: All orders (new and returning customers) Upstack credits to the ad. NULL on days not pulled.

columns.name: upstack_order_revenue
columns.description: Order total of those orders, dollars (tax included, before refunds).

examples.title: Ad level: 30-day spend and Meta-reported ROAS
examples.sql:
SELECT ad_id, ad_name, product_slug,
       round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend,
       sum(meta_purchases) AS purchases,
       round(sum(meta_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS roas
FROM analytics.meta_ad_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3
HAVING sum(spend) > 0
ORDER BY spend DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Ad level: new-customer ROAS and cost per new customer on the Upstack basis (30 days)
examples.sql:
SELECT ad_id, ad_name,
       round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend,
       sum(upstack_new_customers) AS new_customers,
       round(sum(spend) / NULLIF(sum(upstack_new_customers), 0), 2) AS nc_cpa,
       round(sum(upstack_new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS nc_roas
FROM analytics.meta_ad_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30
GROUP BY 1, 2
HAVING sum(spend) > 0
ORDER BY spend DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Spend by product by day (last 14 days)
examples.sql:
SELECT day, coalesce(product_slug, '(no product)') AS product, round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend
FROM analytics.meta_ad_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 14
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1 DESC, 3 DESC;

relations.name: analytics.meta_adset_daily
relations.purpose: Ad set x day roll-up of meta_ad_daily (Meta-reported and Upstack bases side by side).
relations.source: analytics.meta_ad_daily grouped by day and ad set
caveats: Same bases and NULL rules as meta_ad_daily. adset_id is NULL only for legacy family-grain rows (none in production).
An ad set belongs to one campaign; names are the current ones. There is no product column because an ad set can hold ads of several products: group meta_ad_daily by product_slug instead.

columns.name: ads_with_spend
columns.description: Distinct ads in the ad set with spend > 0 that day.

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: Upstack first-time customers credited to the ad set's ads (NULL on days not pulled).

examples.title: Daily spend and Meta ROAS of one campaign's ad sets
examples.sql:
SELECT day, adset_name, round(spend, 2) AS spend, meta_purchases,
       round(meta_revenue / NULLIF(spend, 0), 2) AS roas
FROM analytics.meta_adset_daily
WHERE campaign_id = (SELECT campaign_id FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily ORDER BY day DESC, spend DESC LIMIT 1)
  AND day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 7
ORDER BY day DESC, spend DESC;

examples.title: Ad sets ranked by 7-day new-customer CPA (at least $200 spent)
examples.sql:
SELECT adset_id, max(adset_name) AS adset_name, round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend, sum(upstack_new_customers) AS new_customers,
       round(sum(spend) / NULLIF(sum(upstack_new_customers), 0), 2) AS nc_cpa
FROM analytics.meta_adset_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 7
GROUP BY 1 HAVING sum(spend) >= 200 ORDER BY nc_cpa NULLS LAST LIMIT 25;

relations.name: analytics.meta_campaign_daily
relations.purpose: Campaign x day roll-up of meta_ad_daily (Meta-reported and Upstack bases side by side).
relations.source: analytics.meta_ad_daily grouped by day and campaign
relations.coverage: 2026-05-06 through yesterday (use meta_campaign_daily_history for campaign-level days back to 2024-12-31)
caveats: Same bases and NULL rules as meta_ad_daily.
A campaign can run ads of several products (shared All_US / test campaigns): split by product with meta_ad_daily.

columns.name: adsets_with_spend
columns.description: Distinct ad sets with spend > 0 that day.

columns.name: ads_with_spend
columns.description: Distinct ads with spend > 0 that day.

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: Upstack first-time customers credited to the campaign's ads (NULL on days not pulled).

examples.title: Campaigns, last 7 days: spend, Meta ROAS, NC ROAS
examples.sql:
SELECT campaign_id, max(campaign_name) AS campaign, max(stage) AS stage, round(sum(spend)) AS spend,
       round(sum(meta_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS meta_roas,
       round(sum(upstack_new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS nc_roas
FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 7
GROUP BY 1 HAVING sum(spend) > 0 ORDER BY sum(spend) DESC LIMIT 25;

examples.title: Daily spend, testing vs scaling
examples.sql:
SELECT day, stage, round(sum(spend), 2) AS spend
FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1 DESC, 2;

relations.name: analytics.meta_campaign_daily_history
relations.purpose: Meta campaign x day back to 2024-12-31: the only Meta data before 2026-05-06 (campaign grain, no ad sets or ads). From 2026-05-06 on it equals meta_campaign_daily's Meta-reported columns.
relations.grain: one row per (day, campaign_id) after the day rule (a day is read from 'app' when it has app rows, else from 'sheet')
relations.source: public.proj_feed_meta_day: 'app' = aggregated from ad_daily by the app, 'sheet' = the Lonvera Projections sheet tab 'Meta Campaign - History'
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC via etl.projection_daily); sheet rows never change after the backfill
caveats: Meta-reported only (no Upstack columns). product and stage are classified from the CAMPAIGN NAME here ('VitaBull', 'Beef Liver', 'Boneflex', 'Unclassified'; 'Testing' / 'Scaling'), not through the tracker, so they can differ from analytics.meta_ads.product_slug.
Use it for trends across the May 2026 boundary; the ad-grain views cannot go back that far.

columns.name: product
columns.description: Product guessed from the campaign name: VitaBull | Beef Liver | Boneflex | Unclassified.

columns.name: stage
columns.description: 'Testing' when the campaign name contains 'test', else 'Scaling' (capitalised here).

columns.name: source
columns.description: 'app' (aggregated from ad_daily) or 'sheet' (the sheet's campaign history).

examples.title: Monthly Meta spend by product since 2025
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', day)::date AS month, product, round(sum(spend)) AS spend
FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily_history
WHERE day >= '2025-01-01'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 3 DESC;

examples.title: Meta ROAS by month (Meta-reported)
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', day)::date AS month, round(sum(spend)) AS spend, round(sum(meta_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS roas
FROM analytics.meta_campaign_daily_history GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;

relations.name: analytics.meta_reach
relations.purpose: Account-level reach and frequency for Meta (both ad accounts summed). Reach is de-duplicated by Meta per period, so it is stored at each grain and must never be summed across days or weeks.
relations.grain: one row per (grain, period_key): grain is 'day', 'week' (ISO) or 'month'
relations.source: public.proj_feed_meta_reach (sheet tab 'Meta Account - Reach' today; the feeds service writes a shadow copy in proj_feedx_meta_reach)
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service via etl.projection_daily); the trailing days are replaced
relations.coverage: day 2025-01-01.., week 2024-12-30.., month 2025-01-01..; the current day, week and month are partial
caveats: Account level only: there is NO reach / frequency per ad, ad set, campaign or product (the product table, proj_feed_product_reach, holds unique outbound clicks only).
The last day is today (partial). Compare complete periods only.
frequency = impressions / reach, computed here (NULL when reach is 0).

columns.name: period_end
columns.description: Last day of the period (the current period ends today and is partial).

columns.name: reach
columns.description: People reached over the period (Meta de-duplicated; not additive across periods).

columns.name: unique_link_clicks
columns.description: Unique link clicks over the period.

columns.name: unique_outbound_clicks
columns.description: Unique outbound clicks over the period (Meta de-duplicated).

examples.title: Weekly reach and frequency, last 12 complete weeks
examples.sql:
SELECT period_key, period_start, impressions, reach, frequency
FROM analytics.meta_reach
WHERE grain = 'week' AND period_end < current_date
ORDER BY period_start DESC LIMIT 12;

examples.title: Monthly unique outbound clicks per 1,000 reached
examples.sql:
SELECT period_key, reach, unique_outbound_clicks, round(1000.0 * unique_outbound_clicks / NULLIF(reach, 0), 1) AS uoc_per_1000_reached
FROM analytics.meta_reach WHERE grain = 'month' ORDER BY period_start DESC LIMIT 12;

relations.name: analytics.google_campaign_daily
relations.purpose: Google Ads campaign x day: Google's own spend, impressions, clicks and conversions plus Upstack's attributed new customers / orders. Google has no ad group, ad or keyword grain in this database.
relations.source: public.google_daily (Upstack channel feed joined to Upstack any-click 30-day attribution by campaign name) + upstack_google_campaigns
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC): trailing 7 days re-pulled; the job refuses a day with more than $200 spend and no attributed orders
relations.coverage: Google's own numbers 2024-03-25 through yesterday (Pacific); Upstack columns from 2025-05-13 (NULL before)
caveats: Two bases: google_* are Google's own conversions (restated by Google for days afterwards); upstack_* are Upstack's attribution of orders to the campaign (utm campaign name), any-click 30-day, which credits Google with orders that also had a Meta click.
Purchases and revenue overlap with Meta's: never add google_* or upstack_* to Meta's. Spend, impressions and clicks are additive.
campaign_type is read from the campaign NAME (Shopping, Search, Performance Max, Demand Gen, Other); Upstack exposes none. 'Other' is never guessed.

in_feed = false rows are Upstack-attributed orders whose utm campaign matches no Google campaign ('(not set)', raw ids, deleted campaigns): spend 0, kept so totals tie to Upstack's Google total (about 3% of orders).
clicks are all clicks (Google has no link-click event).

columns.name: campaign_key
columns.description: Google campaign id, or 'name:<utm campaign>' when the utm value is no Google campaign (in_feed = false).

columns.name: campaign_type
columns.description: Shopping | Search | Performance Max | Demand Gen | Other, read from the name.

columns.name: campaign_status
columns.description: Campaign status from the Upstack feed (NULL for in_feed = false rows).

columns.name: bid_strategy
columns.description: Bid strategy from the Upstack feed (NULL for in_feed = false rows).

columns.name: in_feed
columns.description: true = a Google campaign in the channel feed; false = utm campaign with no Google campaign.

columns.name: google_purchases
columns.description: Purchases Google reports (delivered through Upstack's ad-platform feed).

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: First-time customers Upstack credits to the campaign (any-click, 30 days, utm_source 'Google Ads'). NULL before 2025-05-13.

columns.name: upstack_new_customer_revenue
columns.description: Their first-order revenue, dollars (tax included, before refunds).

columns.name: upstack_orders
columns.description: All orders Upstack credits to the campaign.

examples.title: Spend and Google-reported ROAS by campaign type, last 30 days
examples.sql:
SELECT campaign_type, round(sum(spend)) AS spend, round(sum(google_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS google_roas,
       round(sum(upstack_new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(spend), 0), 2) AS nc_roas
FROM analytics.google_campaign_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'google_campaign_daily') - 30
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC;

examples.title: Top Google campaigns by spend this month
examples.sql:
SELECT campaign_name, campaign_type, round(sum(spend)) AS spend, sum(clicks) AS clicks
FROM analytics.google_campaign_daily
WHERE day >= date_trunc('month', current_date - 1)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 15;

relations.name: analytics.platform_daily
relations.purpose: Meta and Google side by side per day. Spend, impressions and clicks are additive across the two platforms; purchases and revenue are not.
relations.grain: one row per (day, platform) with platform 'meta' or 'google'
relations.source: analytics.meta_ad_daily and analytics.google_campaign_daily grouped by day
relations.coverage: Meta 2026-05-06.., Google 2024-03-25.. through yesterday (Pacific); Total NC ROAS is defined only on days both platforms and orders_daily have
caveats: spend is additive: Total spend = sum over platforms. own_purchases / own_revenue / upstack_* are NOT: both platforms credit the same orders (the overlap cannot be measured), so adding them gives the wrong number. Never divide a sum of platform revenue by total spend.
Total NC ROAS = actual new-customer revenue (analytics.orders_daily.new_customer_revenue, counted once) / total spend of the same days. Use the example below.
clicks: Meta = link clicks, Google = all clicks. own_* is each platform's own reporting; upstack_* is Upstack's any-click 30-day attribution.
Meta days are each ad account's own day, Google and Upstack days are Pacific; the one-day offset matters only for the BackUp account (New York).

columns.name: day
columns.description: Calendar day (Meta: ad account day; Google / Upstack: Pacific).

columns.name: spend
columns.description: Platform spend, dollars. Additive across platforms.

columns.name: clicks
columns.description: Meta: link clicks. Google: all clicks.

columns.name: own_purchases
columns.description: Purchases the platform reports itself. Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: own_revenue
columns.description: Conversion value the platform reports itself, dollars. Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: upstack_new_customers
columns.description: Upstack first-time customers credited to the platform (NULL on days Upstack was not pulled). Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: upstack_new_customer_revenue
columns.description: Their first-order revenue, dollars. Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: upstack_orders
columns.description: All orders Upstack credits to the platform. Not additive across platforms.

columns.name: upstack_order_revenue
columns.description: Revenue of those orders, dollars. Not additive across platforms.

examples.title: Meta vs Google spend per day (last 14 days)
examples.sql:
SELECT day,
       round(sum(spend) FILTER (WHERE platform = 'meta'), 2) AS meta_spend,
       round(sum(spend) FILTER (WHERE platform = 'google'), 2) AS google_spend,
       round(sum(spend), 2) AS total_spend
FROM analytics.platform_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 14
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC;

examples.title: Total spend and Total NC ROAS by day (actual new-customer revenue / spend, days both platforms and orders cover)
examples.sql:
WITH s AS (
  SELECT day, sum(spend) AS spend, count(*) AS platforms FROM analytics.platform_daily GROUP BY day
)
SELECT s.day, round(s.spend, 2) AS total_spend, o.new_customer_revenue,
       round(o.new_customer_revenue / NULLIF(s.spend, 0), 4) AS total_nc_roas
FROM s JOIN analytics.orders_daily o USING (day)
WHERE s.platforms = 2 AND s.day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30
ORDER BY s.day DESC;

examples.title: Total NC ROAS for a window (ratio of sums, never a mean of daily ratios)
examples.sql:
WITH s AS (SELECT day, sum(spend) AS spend, count(*) AS platforms FROM analytics.platform_daily GROUP BY day)
SELECT count(*) AS days, round(sum(s.spend)) AS total_spend, round(sum(o.new_customer_revenue)) AS nc_revenue,
       round(sum(o.new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(s.spend), 0), 4) AS total_nc_roas
FROM s JOIN analytics.orders_daily o USING (day)
WHERE s.platforms = 2 AND s.day > (SELECT max(last_day) FROM analytics.data_coverage WHERE source = 'meta_ad_daily') - 30;

relations.name: analytics.orders_daily
relations.purpose: The business's ACTUAL revenue and customers per Pacific day, counted once (Upstack order-level measures). new_customer_revenue is the numerator of Total NC ROAS.
relations.grain: one row per Pacific day with orders
relations.refresh: nightly (etl service 13:00 UTC): trailing 7 days replaced because Upstack restates recent days
caveats: Revenue is the order total as Upstack reports it (tax included), before refunds: all numbers are gross.

There is no product, platform or campaign dimension: you cannot split new-customer revenue by product here. Use the attributed columns of the Meta / Google views (an attribution, not the actual) or the sheet's NC Rev - By Product (proj_feed_nc_product, sheet-fed, not in analytics).
A day with no orders is absent, not zero.
new_customers is the count of first-time customers (first orders).

columns.name: new_customer_revenue
columns.description: Revenue of first orders that day, dollars (tax included, before refunds). orders.new_customer_total_revenue.

columns.name: new_customers
columns.description: Number of new customers (first orders) that day. orders.new_customers.

columns.name: returning_customer_revenue
columns.description: Revenue of repeat orders, dollars (subscription rebills included). orders.returning_customer_total_revenue.

columns.name: orders
columns.description: All orders that day (new and returning). orders.count.

columns.name: loaded_at
columns.description: When the day was last (re)pulled from Upstack.

examples.title: New-customer revenue and new customers by week
examples.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('week', day)::date AS week, round(sum(new_customer_revenue)) AS nc_revenue, sum(new_customers) AS new_customers,
       round(sum(new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(new_customers), 0), 2) AS nc_aov
FROM analytics.orders_daily
WHERE day >= current_date - 90
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC;

examples.title: New vs returning share of revenue, last 30 days
examples.sql:
SELECT round(sum(new_customer_revenue)) AS new_rev, round(sum(returning_customer_revenue)) AS returning_rev,
       round(100 * sum(new_customer_revenue) / NULLIF(sum(total_revenue), 0), 1) AS new_pct
FROM analytics.orders_daily
WHERE day > (SELECT max(day) FROM analytics.orders_daily) - 30;

relations.name: analytics.creative_tracker
relations.purpose: One row per live Creative Tracker row (a concept / ad variant) with its current tag in the product's own tag set, its hook and its since-launch Meta-reported metrics. The way to ask 'which cluster / ICP / pain point / hook performs'.
relations.grain: one row per tracker row (tracker_row_id); an 'ad family' (family_key) can span several rows
relations.source: public.tracker_rows + ad_tags (current) + taxonomy_lines + ad_hooks + ad_metrics + products
relations.refresh: tracker rows synced nightly from the Creative Key Google Sheet (etl service 13:00 UTC); linemap tags and hooks are loaded by hand per tagging cycle (versions dated 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-05)
relations.coverage: all live tracker rows (~3,980); soft-deleted rows are left out
caveats: Metrics (spend_launch ... ads_active_count) sit on the FIRST tracker row of each ad family only; the other rows of the family read 0 (is_first_row says which). So sum over rows is right and a per-row average is wrong. 'Unique ads' = count of distinct family_key.
Since-launch metrics are Meta-reported (Graph API all-time per ad, summed over the family's Meta ads), not Upstack. spend_7d / _30d end on the last complete day.

Tags: products.tag_set decides which set drives the hierarchy: 'linemap' (cluster / ICP / pain point / trigger of the Communication Overview line, read from the creative image or video by a tagger, with a confidence) for Vita Bull, Beef Liver and Boneflex; 'tracker' (the tracker's own columns) for the rest. The tracker_* columns are always the tracker's own tags. A row with no current tag has NULL tag columns.
A family whose tracker rows carry different tags appears under each of them; its spend counts only where its first row sits.
asset_url is a Google Drive link to the creative file; access to the file is governed by Drive, not by this database.

Rows with source 'sheet' / ad_id 'fam:<family>' were a family-grain backfill; none remain in production.
Reach, frequency, video metrics (thruplays, watch time), demographic / placement breakdowns, ad-level budgets and bids are NOT stored.

relations.purpose: ad_daily-shaped table for the Upstack source: Meta's spend / clicks / impressions per ad and day plus the Upstack orders and new customers credited to each ad.

Behind the Test to scale page. Meta's own purchases and revenue; the _upstack_nc / _upstack_all tables read the Upstack attribution. Precomputed (migration 016; it was a view in 015).
relations.grain: one row per family_key that has spend (family_daily rows with spend > 0)

relations.coverage: 2026-05-06 through yesterday; about 2.6K creatives, 610 moved on 2026-11-04
caveats: A move is inferred from daily spend, not from an event: Meta cannot move an ad between campaigns, the buyer duplicates the creative into a scaling campaign. Testing and scaling on the same first day, scaling first and scaling only are NOT moves (see path).

Bulk moves: on 2026-08-22, 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-23 76, 187 and 80 creatives moved in one day (mass relaunches into new scaling campaigns, not test winners). bulk_move_day marks days with 40 or more moves; the app lets you hide them.

first_day is the first day with spend in any stage: creatives already running on the first day of data (launched_before_data_start, 2026-05-06) have an earlier real launch day, so days_in_test is a lower bound.

test_* counts TESTING-stage rows on days before the first scaling day (all testing days when it never scaled); scale_* counts SCALING-stage rows since the move through the last day. Testing spend that continues after the move is test_after_spend only.
Spend and link clicks are Meta's in every view; purchases and revenue are Meta-reported here, Upstack's in the _upstack_ views. Not additive across platforms.
